question: During the Basic Control Skills test, what is scored as a "pull-up"?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_b: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_c: Stopping the vehicle without changing direction
choice_d: Touching a boundary line with the vehicle's mirror
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward during a backing exercise (Exercise 2 or Exercise 4) to clear an encroachment or achieve a better position; the examiner scores the number of times this occurs.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.1 Scoring

question: What is scored as an "encroachment" during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors or unique parts at/above door mirror height
choice_b: Pulling forward to clear an obstruction
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check its position while backing
choice_d: Sounding the horn before shutting off the engine
explanation: An encroachment is touching or crossing an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors (door or fender) or unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height, such as a bucket truck.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.1 Scoring

question: Which action is scored as a "look" during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Pulling forward to gain a better position
choice_b: Sounding the horn to indicate completion of an exercise
choice_c: Opening the door or moving from a seated position to check the vehicle's position while backing
choice_d: Crossing a boundary line with the vehicle's mirror
explanation: A "look" is scored when the driver opens the door or moves from a seated position (or, on a bus, walks to the back to get a better view) while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.1 Scoring

question: What must you do when exiting the vehicle to check its position (a "look") during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Turn off the vehicle's engine and remove the keys before exiting
choice_b: Leave the vehicle in gear so it does not roll
choice_c: Only exit through the passenger-side door
choice_d: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and exit/enter safely while facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact
explanation: The manual requires setting the parking brake, placing the vehicle in neutral/park, and safely exiting/entering by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact (on a bus, facing forward with a firm grasp on the handrail).
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.1 Scoring

question: What may happen if you open your vehicle's door while it is moving (not in neutral/park) during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: It is simply scored as one additional look
choice_b: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_c: It is scored as an encroachment
choice_d: Nothing, as long as the vehicle stops within five seconds
explanation: The manual warns that opening the door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park) may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.1 Scoring

question: How many free looks are you allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing versus Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Three free looks on each exercise
choice_b: Two free looks on Exercise 2 and one free look on Exercise 4
choice_c: No free looks are permitted on either exercise
choice_d: One free look on Exercise 2 and two free looks on Exercise 4
explanation: You may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, to check the vehicle's position.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.1 Scoring

question: What happens if you fail to maneuver your vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner at the end of an exercise?
choice_a: You are given unlimited extra attempts to reposition the vehicle
choice_b: The examiner will reposition the vehicle for you
choice_c: It only counts as one encroachment with no further consequence
choice_d: You will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test
explanation: The manual states that if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner, you will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Control Skills Test general instructions

question: What must you do upon completion of a Basic Control Skills exercise to indicate to the examiner that you are finished?
choice_a: Honk the horn twice and open the driver's door
choice_b: Simply raise your hand out the window
choice_c: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, sound the horn, and shut off the engine
choice_d: Turn on the four-way emergency flashers
explanation: Upon completing an exercise, the driver must set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, sound the horn, and shut off the engine to indicate completion.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Control Skills Test general instructions

question: What could result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act during the Basic Control Skills test, according to the example given in the manual?
choice_a: Asking the examiner to clarify the instructions
choice_b: Taking slightly longer than average to complete an exercise
choice_c: Forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while the vehicle is in motion
choice_d: Using a free pull-up during Exercise 2
explanation: The manual gives forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion as examples of an "unsafe act" that may result in automatic failure and termination of the test.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, how many times are you allowed to stop the vehicle?
choice_a: As many times as needed to line up correctly
choice_b: Up to three times
choice_c: Only once
choice_d: Up to two times
explanation: For Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, the manual states you may stop only once while judging the front of your vehicle during the controlled stop.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, how far must you back the vehicle?
choice_a: Until signaled to stop by a passenger
choice_b: A distance of exactly three feet
choice_c: Until the rear of the vehicle touches the alley's back wall
choice_d: Straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end
explanation: For Exercise 2, you back straight through the alley until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How many free pull-ups are allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and how many times may you exit the vehicle to check around it?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and two exits to check around the vehicle
choice_b: One free pull-up and one exit to check around the vehicle
choice_c: Three free pull-ups and no exits allowed
choice_d: Zero free pull-ups and one exit to check around the vehicle
explanation: On Exercise 2, you are allowed one free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around it.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: In Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, which of the following is true?
choice_a: You are allowed two free pull-ups if you clip a cone
choice_b: You are allowed to stop once to reposition before continuing
choice_c: You are NOT allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle during the exercise, and if you stop, the exercise ends
choice_d: You may exit the vehicle once to check your tracking position
explanation: The manual states that during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, you are NOT allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle; if you stop, the exercise will be ended.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, how close must the rear-most part of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Within three (3) feet
choice_b: It must touch the rear boundary exactly
choice_c: Within one (1) foot
choice_d: Within ten (10) feet
explanation: In Exercise 4, you must bring the rear-most part of the vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley and stop in the three-foot box.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Unlimited pull-ups but no exits
choice_b: Two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits to check around the vehicle
choice_c: Three free pull-ups and three exits
choice_d: One free pull-up and one exit to check around the vehicle
explanation: On Exercise 4, you are allowed two free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around it.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: If you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, what must you do?
choice_a: Continue backing until told to stop by a bystander
choice_b: Pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, then resume the exercise
choice_c: Immediately fail the test with no option to continue
choice_d: Exit the vehicle and manually reposition the cones
explanation: The manual states that if you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley, you must pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must be true before you can proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: You must wait 24 hours after the Basic Control Skills test
choice_b: There is no prerequisite; the Road Test can be taken at any time
choice_c: You must first pass the Basic Control Skills test
choice_d: You must complete a written re-test on backing maneuvers
explanation: The manual explicitly states that the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before you can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 12, Road Test transition note

question: During the On-Road Driving test, what is required of you at all times?
choice_a: Keep one hand on the horn at all times
choice_b: Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs/signals/laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation
choice_c: Drive only in the left-most lane for the entire route
choice_d: Maintain a constant speed regardless of posted limits
explanation: The manual requires that you wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the Kansas CDL manual, when does "unsafe coasting" occur while approaching a turn?
choice_a: Anytime you release the accelerator pedal
choice_b: When you shift gears while stopped at an intersection
choice_c: When your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
choice_d: When you use your turn signal more than 100 feet before the turn
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.1 Turns

question: As you approach an intersection where you must stop, what must your vehicle NOT do?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop behind the stop line
choice_b: Decelerate gently before stopping
choice_c: Roll forward or backward
choice_d: Maintain a safe gap behind the vehicle in front
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must not roll forward or backward when stopped at an intersection.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what should you avoid doing?
choice_a: Checking traffic thoroughly in all directions
choice_b: Yielding to pedestrians in the intersection
choice_c: Keeping your hands on the wheel
choice_d: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
explanation: The manual instructs that you should not change lanes while proceeding through an intersection.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the road test, where should your vehicle be positioned and how should your speed be managed?
choice_a: As far right as possible even if it means driving on the shoulder
choice_b: Straddling the center lane markings for better visibility
choice_c: Centered in the right-most lane, keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_d: Centered in the left-most lane at maximum posted speed
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper (right-most) lane, keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: When required to stop at a railroad crossing (e.g., driving a bus or a vehicle displaying placards), how far from the nearest rail must you stop?
choice_a: Exactly 25 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: As close as possible, with no minimum distance specified
choice_c: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual instructs drivers required to stop at railroad crossings to stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: While any part of your vehicle is crossing railroad tracks, what must you NOT do?
choice_a: Keep your hands on the steering wheel
choice_b: Deactivate the four-way flashers after fully crossing
choice_c: Stop, change gears, or change lanes
choice_d: Continue checking mirrors and traffic
explanation: The manual states you should not stop, change gears, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is proceeding across the tracks.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: When performing a student discharge for a School Bus endorsement, how far from the students must the school bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 10 feet away from the students at the stop
choice_b: No minimum distance is specified
choice_c: At least 25 feet away from the students at the stop
choice_d: Exactly 5 feet away from the students
explanation: The manual states that when stopping for student discharge, the school bus must come to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: If your commercial vehicle has an unsynchronized manual transmission, what must you do when shifting?
choice_a: Double-clutch when shifting
choice_b: Coast with the clutch depressed between shifts
choice_c: Ride the clutch to control speed on grades
choice_d: Rev the engine before every shift to match RPMs
explanation: The manual requires that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, you must double-clutch when shifting, and you should not rev or lug the engine, ride the clutch, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage

question: Which of the following is a proper brake usage behavior evaluated during the road test?
choice_a: Brake smoothly using steady pressure, without riding or pumping the brake
choice_b: Ride the brake lightly down long grades to control speed
choice_c: Pump the brake repeatedly when approaching a stop
choice_d: Brake harshly to come to a complete stop as quickly as possible
explanation: The manual states that under Brake Usage, drivers must not ride or pump the brake and must not brake harshly, instead braking smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: For the Stop/Start maneuver, you are asked to pull over as if to check something on the vehicle. Which of the following is part of the required procedure once stopped?
choice_a: Leave the engine running in gear with your foot on the brake
choice_b: Turn off the four-way flashers before coming to a stop
choice_c: Immediately exit the vehicle without setting the parking brake
choice_d: Activate the four-way emergency flashers and apply the parking brake
explanation: Once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver, the manual requires activating the four-way emergency flashers, applying the parking brake, and moving the gear shift to neutral or park.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 13, 13.1.6 Stop/Start
